momentumDashboard.methodBody: Daily data for assets in the watchlist, updated after the close. Period returns and daily changes use adjusted closing prices, reflecting dividend and split adjustments. Momentum ranks 20-, 60- and 120-session returns within each list, weighted 20%, 40% and 40%. Group scores average their assets.
momentumDashboard.methodTrend: Group lines show average momentum scores. Asset relative strength lines divide adjusted prices by SPY prices, normalized to 100 at the start, with a 20-session simple moving average. Rankings use the latest SPY data date; assets missing that date are excluded. Stock scores use a shared pool of SPY constituents and available USD equity holdings from ETFs, with the same 20/60/120-session weights. RSI uses 14-session Wilder smoothing. Average daily turnover estimates close times volume over 20 sessions.
momentumDashboard.methodCaveat: Scores describe past relative performance. They do not predict future returns or constitute trading recommendations.
momentumDashboard.guideLabel: How to read and use this page

period.title: Reading the tiles and lines
period.body: Tiles show the average score of each group; dark green indicates stronger momentum. Lines show average scores over the past 60 trading days. A rising line means the group is gaining relative strength; a falling line means it is weakening.

score.title: What the momentum score means
score.body: Assets that have performed strongly may continue to lead over the medium term. Scores combine performance over 20, 60 and 120 trading days, roughly 1, 3 and 6 months. Assets that rose more, or fell less, score higher. Each list ranks its assets separately.

action.title: Find stronger assets
action.body: Start with a stronger group, then review its highest-ranked assets. Select an asset row to compare returns and its lead over SPY across periods. The relative strength line shows whether it continues to outperform the broad market.

momentumDashboard.researchLink: Research this asset on Yahoo Finance
momentumDashboard.relativeTrendAria: {{symbol}} relative strength versus SPY and its 20-session moving average.
momentumDashboard.relativeTrendHelp: A rising line means the asset is outperforming SPY; a falling line means it is underperforming. A line above a rising 20-session average helps identify assets that continue to lead.
momentumDashboard.staleAsset: Latest-session data is incomplete. This asset is temporarily excluded from momentum rankings.
momentumDashboard.rsiHelp: RSI measures short-term price strength. During a pullback, compare it with momentum scores and the relative strength line.
momentumDashboard.liquidityHelp: Estimated daily trading value. Higher turnover generally makes trading easier.

momentumDashboard.coverageBody: This curated watchlist consists mainly of US-listed ETFs, plus other listed products such as the DXYZ closed-end fund. It covers sectors, themes, stock markets, bonds, commodities and equity strategies, not the entire market. Some assets appear in multiple lists.
momentumDashboard.coverageGroups: Groups reflect research themes, not an official industry classification. Group scores depend on the assets included. ETFs can hold the same stocks, so adding more funds does not necessarily broaden coverage.

groupHints.equal-weighted-sectors: Equal stock weights within each sector
groupHints.factors: Momentum, quality, low volatility and more

groupDescriptions.factors: Factors are characteristics used to select stocks. This group includes momentum (SPMO), high market sensitivity (SPHB), quality (SPHQ), low volatility (SPLV), and high dividends with low volatility (SPHD). The tile averages these different strategies.
groupDescriptions.growth: These funds select stocks with growth characteristics, such as earnings or revenue growth, according to their index rules. They cover large and small companies. Growth describes the selection style, not a promise that prices will rise.
groupDescriptions.broad: Compare the total market, large, mid, small and micro caps, and concentrated portfolios such as MAGS. Diversification differs across these funds.
groupDescriptions.equal-weighted-sectors: Each stock within a sector receives the same weight at index rebalancing; weights then drift as prices change.
groupDescriptions.market-cap-weighted-sectors: Larger companies generally receive larger weights within a sector, subject to each index’s rules.

assetDescriptions.SPLV: Low volatility · lower past price variability

screen.title: Explore markets or find stocks
screen.body: Market overview compares groups and ETFs. Stock screener finds candidates within strong sectors. Switch between the two at any time.

scope.title: Choose a market to compare
scope.body: “Sectors & themes” compares sectors, “Major assets” compares stocks, bonds and commodities, and “Market structure” compares stock-selection approaches. Switch between recent momentum and daily change.

map.title: Select a group to see its ETFs
map.body: Tiles show each group’s average momentum score. Higher scores mean stronger performance over recent months. Select a group to see its ETFs below.

mapDaily.title: Select a group to see its ETFs
mapDaily.body: Daily change shows each group’s move in the latest trading session: green for gains and red for losses. Select a group to see its ETFs below.

asset.title: Open an ETF to compare performance
asset.body: Select an ETF row to see its performance and charts. Open Constituents to explore its stocks, then return to the list to compare other assets.

screen.pullbackExplanation: Among strong candidates, find stocks whose prices have retreated and whose recent gains and losses are more balanced. Watch whether they retain their lead before assessing an entry.
screen.oversoldExplanation: Among strong candidates, find stocks with stronger recent selling pressure. Their prices can keep falling; watch for the decline to stop before assessing an entry.
screen.oversoldCaution: Prices can keep falling while RSI is low. Watch for the decline to stop before assessing an entry.
